checks.method: Read the frozen manuscript, admission declaration, and the three successful audit receipts; compared explicit theorem types with the stated research question.
checks.observation: The Profile A audit prints I(27) implies nonrealizability of A; the terminal audit supplies B exclusion and I(27) implies G(80). Thus this is not merely an implication retaining both A/B exclusions as undischarged premises. No completed source-closure replay is inferred.

checks.method: Recomputed degree sums and followed the stated reduction from G(81) plus the exhaustive 81-member dichotomy to G(80).
checks.observation: Both profiles have 17 supported points and total degree 324: 20+16·19=324 and 2·20+14·19+18=324=4·81. Excluding both profiles under I(27) removes the only equality case of the inherited upper bound 81; integrality then yields 80. The external I(27) theorem is needed only to instantiate this implication for the ordinary global corollary.

checks.method: Matched Theorem 1 to the fully printed two-star theorem and examined its independence from the Profile B support/degree census.
checks.observation: The printed theorem quantifies over arbitrary Type u and Finset families without I(27), a fixed support, or a degree-eighteen point. Its result is therefore broader than literal Profile B exclusion while remaining fixed rank four. The general all-rank sunflower conjecture is not implied.

findings.disposition: Maintain this separation through the final version; no revision required in the current framing.
findings.statement: The inspected printed terminal proposition contains I(27) as a universally quantified antecedent, whereas the printed independent-twenty-stars root contains only uniformity, sunflower-freeness, distinct centers, exact degrees and noncooccurrence. This supports the manuscript's distinction between conditional global formal theorem and unconditional structural theorem.

content.summary: The question is substantial and correctly framed: the manuscript supplies both actual-family boundary exclusions and a separate unrestricted two-star theorem. The global Lean theorem remains conditional on I(27), while the numerical G(80) deduction is explicitly an ordinary corollary using external computational mathematics. Admission to substantive review is justified; acceptance awaits the later proof, source and reproducibility phases.
